title: The Gruffalo
logline: A little mouse walks through the wood and invents a monster to scare the other animals — then the monster appears.
why: The narration is one short rhyming line per picture, and the same invitation comes back three times, so a beginner can follow the pattern without catching every word. The story is a simple chain of who the mouse meets next, which students can retell with four or five short sentences.
language: Clear British narration in rhyme, read slowly, with polite short lines from the fox, the owl and the snake; the gruffalo speaks in a deep, slow voice.
content: Very mild cartoon peril: a big monster follows a small mouse through the wood, but nobody is hurt. Suitable for all ages.

scenes.title: The fox's invitation
scenes.task: Pause when the fox speaks. Where does the fox live, and what food does he offer? Answer in one short sentence.

scenes.title: Tea in the treetops
scenes.task: The owl invites the mouse for tea. Listen for three food or drink words and write them down.

scenes.title: Draw the monster
scenes.task: Pause and draw the animal the mouse describes: eyes, tongue, back, nose. Compare your drawing with the next picture.

scenes.title: Who is afraid now?
scenes.task: The real gruffalo walks behind the mouse. Stop here and predict: what will the fox, the owl and the snake do?

words.ex: The mouse walks through the wood.

words.def: a wild animal with red fur
words.ex: The fox invites the mouse to lunch.
The owl lives in a tall tree.

words.def: a long animal with no legs
words.ex: The snake slides out of the grass.
The animals are afraid of the gruffalo.
The mouse is small but clever.

questions: What does the mouse say to the fox? Try to say it in a big, brave voice.
Why do the fox, the owl and the snake run away at the end?
The mouse describes orange eyes and a black tongue. What colour are the gruffalo's eyes in the film?
Is the mouse clever or lucky? Give one example from the film.
Which animal do you like best: the fox, the owl or the snake? Why?
Would you like to walk in a dark wood at night? What would you take with you?
In your country, what animal stories do parents tell children? Is there a big monster in them?
Which line from the film do you like best? Say it the same way as the mouse.

gaps.line: A mouse took a stroll through the deep dark ___.
Come and have lunch in my underground ___.
It's terribly kind of you, Fox, but ___.
He has terrible tusks and terrible ___.
The mouse found a nut and the nut was ___.

quotes.quote: Come and have lunch in my underground house.
quotes.note: The fox is the first animal the mouse meets, and the first to hear about the gruffalo.

quotes.quote: It's terribly kind of you, Fox, but no.
quotes.note: The mouse is always polite, and always says no.

quotes.quote: A gruffalo? What's a gruffalo?
quotes.note: All three animals ask this; the fox asks it first.

quiz.q: Who does the mouse meet first?
quiz.why: The fox finds the mouse first and invites him to lunch.

quiz.q: Where does the owl live?
quiz.why: The owl asks the mouse up to her house in the tree.

quiz.q: Which animal does the mouse meet last?
quiz.why: The snake is the third animal, just before the gruffalo appears.

quiz.q: Why do the animals run away?
options: They see the gruffalo behind the mouse
quiz.why: The mouse walks in front, so the animals see the monster and not the small mouse.

quiz.q: What does the mouse find at the end?
quiz.why: After all the danger he finds a nut, and the nut is good.

roleplay.title: The three invitations
roleplay.setting: The deep dark wood, in the afternoon. The mouse is walking home and one hungry animal stops him.

roles.brief: You are small and polite. You do not want to be lunch, so you invent a big friend who is coming to meet you.
You are hungry and friendly. Your house is underground and you have lunch ready. You believe everything you hear.
You live in a tree and you want tea. You are not sure about this monster, so you ask a lot of questions.

roleplay.challenge: Play it three times, once with each animal. The mouse must use the same three sentences every time and change only the animal's name.

quest.title: Station 1 · Draw the monster
quest.task: Find the moment the mouse describes the gruffalo. Write the three colours he uses for the eyes, the tongue and the back.
quest.answer: orange eyes, black tongue, purple prickles

quest.title: Station 2 · Word hunt
quest.task: Find in the film: a place with many trees, a bird awake at night, and a long animal with no legs.

quest.title: Station 3 · Your own monster
quest.task: Invent a monster for your classroom. Describe it in three short sentences: eyes, food, home.

quest.title: Station 4 · Who comes first?
quest.task: Put these four in order: the gruffalo, the fox, the snake, the owl.

title: Room on the Broom
logline: A witch and her cat fly on a broom, and every animal they meet asks for a ride — but the broom is getting full.
why: The same question and the same answer come back four times, so a beginner hears the pattern enough to say it too. Hat, bow, wand and broom are easy nouns to point at, and the animals' faces show every feeling without a word.
language: Rhyming British narration with a short repeated question and answer; the witch speaks slowly and kindly, and the dragon has a loud, low voice.
content: A dragon chases the witch and says he wants to eat her, which may frighten very young children; the animals trick him and nobody is hurt.

scenes.title: The wind takes the hat
scenes.task: Pause when the hat flies away. Which animal brings it back, and what does that animal want?

scenes.title: A new passenger
scenes.task: Listen for the question the new animal asks. Clap every time you hear the word 'room'.

scenes.title: The broom is full
scenes.task: Five of them are on the broom and the wind is strong. Pause and predict: what will happen to the broom?

scenes.title: The mud monster
scenes.task: The animals cover themselves in mud. Why is this clever, and who are they hiding from?

words.ex: The witch flies on a broom.

words.def: a brush on a long stick
words.ex: Four animals sit on the broom.
The frog finds the witch's wand.
The wind takes the witch's hat.

words.def: a big animal that breathes fire
words.ex: The dragon wants the witch for dinner.
The animals put mud on their faces.

questions: What does the wind take first: the hat, the bow or the wand?
The cat is not happy about the new animals. Do you understand him? Why?
Why does the witch say yes to every animal? Would you say yes?
How do the animals save the witch from the dragon? Was it a good plan?
Would you get on a broom with four animals? Why or why not?
In your country, is there a story about a witch? What does she look like?
Which animal would you like to be in this story? Say why in three sentences.
Which line in the film is easy to say? Try it with the same voice as the witch.

gaps.line: As long as there's ___ on the broom.
The dog brings back the witch's ___.
gaps.hint: you wear it on your head

gaps.line: The frog finds the witch's ___.
The cat and the witch ___ in the sky.
The dragon is big and very ___.

quotes.quote: As long as there's room on the broom.
quotes.note: The witch says it every time, and the broom gets fuller.

quotes.quote: Is there room on the broom for a dog like me?
quotes.note: Every animal asks the same question; the dog is the first.

quotes.quote: Is there room on the broom for a bird like me?
quotes.note: The bird asks second, and she is the one who finds the bow.

quiz.q: What does the wind blow off first?
quiz.why: The hat goes first, then the bow, then the wand.

quiz.q: Who finds the witch's bow?
quiz.why: The bird picks up the bow and asks for a ride.

quiz.q: What does the witch say to every animal?
quiz.why: She always says yes while there is room on the broom.

quiz.q: Why does the broom break?
options: Too many animals sit on it
quiz.why: Five of them are on one broom in a strong wind.

quiz.q: How do the animals stop the dragon?
quiz.why: Covered in mud, they look like a horrible beast and the dragon runs off.

roleplay.title: The full broom
roleplay.setting: In the sky on a very small broom. The wind is strong and the cat wants his space back.

roles.brief: You are kind and say yes to everyone. You have no more space, but you cannot say no.
You were here first. You are grumpy, you count the passengers, and you hold on very tight.
You have the hat in your mouth and you really want a ride. You are friendly and a little bit silly.

roleplay.challenge: Add one more animal at the end with a new question and a new sound. The witch must still say yes, and the cat must count everyone.

quest.title: Station 1 · Lost and found
quest.task: Find which animal brings back the hat, the bow and the wand, in that order.
quest.answer: the dog, the bird, the frog

quest.title: Station 2 · Word puzzle
quest.task: Which lost thing do you wear? Which one is for magic? Which one is a brush on a stick?
quest.answer: the hat, the wand, the broom

quest.title: Station 3 · New passenger
quest.task: Draw a new animal for the broom. Write three sentences: what it finds, what it asks, what it can do.

quest.title: Station 4 · Count them
quest.task: How many of them fly on the new broom at the end? Count and write the number and the names.
quest.answer: five: witch, cat, dog, bird, frog

title: Stick Man
logline: A stick who lives in a family tree goes out for a run and is carried far away from home.
why: The story is a simple chain of who takes Stick Man next, told in rhyme with one line he repeats, so students can retell it as a list. Every new place gives a concrete noun to name: river, nest, snow, fire.
language: Warm British narration in rhyme, with a few shouted lines from Stick Man; the animals and the people speak very little.
content: Mild danger: Stick Man is almost burned in a fireplace on Christmas Eve before he is saved. Nothing frightening for young children.

scenes.title: A dog wants a stick
scenes.task: Pause when the dog takes Stick Man. What does the dog want to play? Show the action with your hands.

scenes.title: Into the water
scenes.task: Stick Man is in the river. Pause and predict: who will pick him up next?

scenes.title: Cold and far from home
scenes.task: It is winter and Stick Man is lost. Say three words for how he feels, then three words for the weather.

scenes.title: Santa in the chimney
scenes.task: Santa finds Stick Man in the fireplace. Retell the last two minutes in three short sentences.

words.ex: The dog runs away with the stick.
The swan puts Stick Man in her nest.

words.def: water that moves to the sea
words.ex: The girl throws him into the river.

words.def: a seat that slides on snow
words.ex: Santa's sleigh flies through the night.
Stick Man is almost on the fire.
Stick Man wants to go home.

questions: Who takes Stick Man first, and what does that animal do with him?
Why does the swan want Stick Man? Is she kind to him?
Stick Man says the same thing many times. What is it? Say it with feeling.
Why is Christmas Eve a dangerous night for a stick?
Would you like to be a stick for one day? What would be good and what would be bad?
In your country, what do families do on Christmas Eve? Do you have a special tree?
Stick Man's family waits for him. How do they feel at the end?
Which line from the film can you say by heart now? Say it to your partner.

gaps.line: I'm Stick Man, I'm Stick Man, I'm Stick Man, that's ___!
Stick Man lives in the family ___.
The dog wants to play with the ___.
Santa takes Stick Man home in his ___.
Stick Man has three stick ___.

quotes.quote: I'm Stick Man, I'm Stick Man, I'm Stick Man, that's me!
quotes.note: He says it when someone picks him up, to explain who he is.

quotes.quote: I want to go home to my family tree.
quotes.note: This is what he wants through the whole film.

quotes.quote: Stick Man lives in the family tree.
quotes.note: The narrator opens the story with this line.

quiz.q: Where does Stick Man live?
quiz.why: He lives in the family tree with his family.

quiz.q: Who takes Stick Man away to play?
quiz.why: A dog picks him up and runs off with him.

quiz.q: What does the swan use Stick Man for?
quiz.why: She puts him in her nest, and he cannot move.

quiz.q: Who saves Stick Man on Christmas Eve?
quiz.why: Santa comes down the chimney and takes him home in the sleigh.

quiz.q: How does Stick Man feel at the end?
quiz.why: He is back in the family tree with his family.

roleplay.title: Lost in the snow
roleplay.setting: A cold night, far from home. Stick Man is stuck in the snow and a child finds him.

roles.brief: You are polite and tired. You want to go home, but nobody understands you.
You want a stick for your snowman's arm. You do not know that this stick can talk.
You are in a hurry and your sleigh is full. You are kind, but you have no time to lose.

roleplay.challenge: The child must not hear Stick Man speak. Play it once as a funny scene and once as a sad one.

quest.title: Station 1 · Who takes him?
quest.task: Find three animals or people who take Stick Man before Santa does, in the right order.
quest.answer: the dog, the girl, the swan

quest.title: Station 2 · One word, three times
quest.task: Stick Man says one word three times in the same line. What is the word, and what is the whole line?
quest.answer: Stick Man: I'm Stick Man, I'm Stick Man, I'm Stick Man, that's me

quest.title: Station 3 · A letter home
quest.task: Write three short sentences as Stick Man to his family: where you are, what happened, what you want.

quest.title: Station 4 · Count the family
quest.task: How many stick children are in the family tree? Write the number and the four family words.
quest.answer: three children, with Stick Man and Stick Lady Love

title: The Snowman
logline: A boy builds a snowman on Christmas Eve, and at midnight the snowman comes alive and takes him flying.
why: There is no dialogue at all — the song and the pictures carry everything, so nobody has to follow fast speech. The trip gives a clear order of events (garden, house, sky, party, morning), which is exactly the narration A1 students can produce.
language: No spoken dialogue. One song, sung in a clear high voice, over an orchestral score; the only words on screen are small labels.
content: Gentle and sad rather than frightening: the snowman melts in the morning, which can upset small children.

scenes.title: Snow in the garden
scenes.task: Pause on the finished snowman. Name everything the boy uses — hat, scarf, nose, buttons — and say what each one is made of.

scenes.title: Midnight
scenes.task: Listen to the music when the snowman moves. Is it fast or slow, happy or strange? Show your answer with your hand.

scenes.title: Walking in the air
scenes.task: Pause on the flying picture. Where are they now? Describe the land under them in two sentences.

scenes.title: At the party
scenes.task: Count the snowmen at the party. What is different about each one? Who do they meet?

words.def: soft white pieces from the sky
words.ex: The garden is white with snow.
The boy builds a big snowman.

words.def: long warm cloth for your neck
words.ex: Father Christmas gives the boy a scarf.
At midnight the snowman comes alive.
They fly over the sea.

words.def: to turn soft and become water
words.ex: In the morning the snowman melts.

questions: What does the boy put on the snowman? Name three things.
The snowman walks around the house at night. Which room do you like best, and why?
Why does the snowman stand in the cold freezer? What does this tell you about him?
Would you go flying with a snowman? What would you be afraid of?
Father Christmas gives the boy a scarf and a card. Why does the boy keep the scarf?
In your country, does it snow at Christmas? What do children build in winter?
How does the boy feel in the morning? Is the ending happy or sad for you?
There are no words in this film. Which line from the song can you sing or say?

gaps.line: We're walking in the ___.
We're floating in the moonlit ___.
The people far ___ are sleeping as we fly.
At midnight the snowman comes ___.
In the morning the snowman ___.

quotes.quote: We're walking in the air.
quotes.note: Nobody speaks in this film; the words come from the song.

quotes.quote: I'm holding very tight.
quotes.note: The singer describes what the boy is doing as they fly.

quotes.quote: The people far below are sleeping as we fly.
quotes.note: It is the middle of the night and the houses under them are dark.

quiz.q: When does the snowman come alive?
quiz.why: The clock shows twelve and the snowman starts to move.

quiz.q: What do the boy and the snowman do first?
quiz.why: They go quietly through the house and look at everything.

quiz.q: Where do they fly?
quiz.why: They fly over the sea to a party in the snow.

quiz.q: What does Father Christmas give the boy?
quiz.why: He gives him a card and a scarf with a snowman on it.

quiz.q: What is in the garden in the morning?
options: A scarf and some melted snow
quiz.why: The snowman has melted, but the scarf shows that the night was real.

roleplay.title: The midnight guest
roleplay.setting: A dark kitchen at midnight. The boy hears a noise downstairs and finds his snowman at the window.

roles.brief: You are surprised but brave. You whisper, because your parents are asleep upstairs.
You have no words at all. You show everything with your hands, your head and your face.
You are upstairs and half asleep. You call down once or twice and then go back to bed.

roleplay.challenge: The snowman has no lines: everything must be acted. The boy says the words for both of them.

quest.title: Station 1 · What is left?
quest.task: Find the last shot. Write everything that is left in the snow, and say what each thing was part of the snowman.
quest.answer: hat, scarf, coal eyes, tangerine nose, buttons

quest.title: Station 2 · Song words
quest.task: Find a word in the song for the space above us, and a word for the space under us.

quest.title: Station 3 · Draw the flight
quest.task: Draw the flight. Write three sentences: who flies, where they go, what they see.

quest.title: Station 4 · Time order
quest.task: Put these four moments in order: the flight, the morning, midnight, building the snowman.

title: A Charlie Brown Christmas
logline: Charlie Brown is sad at Christmas, so he looks for the true meaning of the holiday and finds a very small tree.
why: The children speak in short, clear American sentences and repeat the same feelings again and again, so beginners get useful emotion words almost for free. The story is slow, the pictures are simple, and the ending is easy to tell in three sentences.
language: Slow, clear American English with children's voices and jazz music; a few words in the Bible reading are unusual and worth teaching before you watch.
content: A gentle story about feeling sad at Christmas. One character reads the Christmas story from the Bible. Nothing violent.

scenes.title: Charlie Brown is sad
scenes.task: Pause after the first scene. Charlie Brown says he is not happy. Why? Write three words for feelings.

scenes.title: The little tree
scenes.task: Pause on the tree. How many branches has it got? What colour is it? Why do the other children laugh?

scenes.title: Linus speaks
scenes.task: Listen to Linus. What is he telling the others, and why does everyone go quiet?

scenes.title: One small decoration
scenes.task: The children decorate the tree. Retell what happens in three short sentences.

words.ex: Charlie Brown is sad at Christmas.
The little tree has only four branches.
The children want big presents.
The children decorate the little tree.
Charlie Brown feels lonely at Christmas.

words.def: to make music with your voice
words.ex: The children sing at the end.

questions: Why is Charlie Brown sad at the start? Do you ever feel like that?
Lucy wants presents for Christmas. What do you want this year, and why?
Charlie Brown chooses a very small tree. Is it a good choice or a bad choice?
Why do the other children laugh at his tree?
Linus says what Christmas is really about. What is important for you at Christmas?
Would you like to be in the play? Which part would you choose?
In your country, what do people do at Christmas or at your big winter holiday?
Which line from Charlie Brown do you like? Say it with a sad voice, then a happy one.

gaps.line: Good ___!
gaps.hint: an old way to say 'oh no'

gaps.line: Christmas is coming, but I'm not ___.
I know nobody ___ me.
Isn't there anyone who knows what Christmas is all ___?
Merry Christmas, Charlie ___!

quotes.quote: Good grief!
quotes.note: His famous line — he says it when something goes wrong.

quotes.quote: Isn't there anyone who knows what Christmas is all about?
quotes.note: He shouts it in the middle of the play practice.

quotes.quote: Sure, Charlie Brown, I can tell you what Christmas is all about.
quotes.note: Linus then tells the story of the first Christmas.

quiz.q: Why is Charlie Brown unhappy?
options: He does not feel the Christmas feeling
quiz.why: He says Christmas is coming but he is not happy.

quiz.q: Who asks Charlie Brown to direct the play?
quiz.why: Lucy thinks he needs a job, so she gives him the play.

quiz.q: What tree does Charlie Brown buy?
quiz.why: He chooses a small, thin real tree, and the others laugh.

quiz.q: What does Snoopy do in the film?
quiz.why: Snoopy enters a house decoration contest and wins first prize.

quiz.q: How does the film end?
options: Everyone sings and the tree looks beautiful
quiz.why: The children decorate the little tree and sing together.

roleplay.title: The Christmas play
roleplay.setting: A cold hall. The children are practising a play and nobody knows what to do next.

roles.brief: You are the director and you are nervous. You want the play to be right, and nobody listens to you.
You want the biggest part in the play. You are bossy and you give orders.
You are calm. You carry your blanket everywhere and you say the one thing everybody needs to hear.

roleplay.challenge: Use no props except a chair and a bag. Play the scene twice: once with everyone shouting, once with everyone quiet.

quest.title: Station 1 · One little tree
quest.task: Find the moment Charlie Brown chooses his tree. Write one word for its size and one word for its colour.

quest.title: Station 2 · Feeling words
quest.task: Find three feeling words in the film and write one sentence with each.

quest.title: Station 3 · A card for Charlie Brown
quest.task: Write a short card to Charlie Brown in three sentences. Use one feeling word and one present.

quest.title: Station 4 · Put it in order
quest.task: Order these four moments: Linus speaks, the tree falls at home, Charlie Brown buys the tree, the children sing.
quest.answer: buys the tree, Linus speaks, the tree falls, the singing

title: Piper
logline: A tiny sandpiper is afraid of the sea, until a hermit crab shows her how to look under the water.
why: Six minutes, no dialogue, and one clear problem: a little bird who is scared of water. Students can watch it twice and narrate every shot — who, where, and what happens next — with words they already have.
language: No dialogue at all: music, wind, water and bird sounds. The students supply the words, so the film suits a class that is still shy about speaking.
content: A big wave knocks the little bird over and she is wet and frightened for a moment; there is nothing else to worry about.

scenes.title: Mum goes to eat
scenes.task: Pause when the mother flies to the water. What does she eat? Point to it on the screen.

scenes.title: The big wave
scenes.task: The little bird stands near the water. Pause before the wave: what will happen? Guess first, then watch.

scenes.title: The crab's idea
scenes.task: The crab shows her something. What is it, and why does it help her find food?

scenes.title: Food for everyone
scenes.task: At the end the other birds follow her. Tell the ending in three sentences: who, what, why.

words.def: an animal with wings and feathers
words.ex: The little bird has soft brown feathers.

words.def: very small stones on a beach
words.ex: The birds run on the wet sand.

words.def: water that moves onto the beach
words.ex: A big wave hits the little bird.
Her feathers are wet after the wave.

words.def: a small animal with a shell
words.ex: The crab digs into the sand.
At the end the little bird is brave.

questions: Why does the little bird not want to go to the water?
What does the wave do to her? Show the moment with your hands.
How does the crab help her? What does she learn to do?
Would you go back into the sea if a big wave knocked you down? Why or why not?
Which animal is the best teacher in this film? Say why.
In your country, do children learn to swim? At what age?
The film has no words. What did the music tell you?
If you gave the little bird one line to say, what would it be?

gaps.line: The little bird is afraid of the ___.
gaps.hint: the sea is full of it

gaps.line: A big ___ hits her.
gaps.hint: water that moves to the beach

gaps.line: The crab digs in the ___.
gaps.hint: it is under your feet on a beach

gaps.line: Open your ___ and look!
Her mother brings her ___ at the start.

quotes.quote: No words: the mother leaves the nest and flies to the sea.
quotes.note: Piper has no dialogue, so read each moment as one short sentence and ask who does it.

quotes.quote: No words: a big wave covers her and she is wet all over.
quotes.note: She is not hurt, but she is very scared of the water now.

quotes.quote: No words: she digs in the sand with her beak and finds food.
quotes.note: She copies what the crab does, and it works.

quiz.q: What animal is the star of the film?
quiz.why: She is a baby sandpiper, a small bird that lives by the sea.

quiz.q: What is she afraid of?
quiz.why: A wave knocks her over, and after that she will not go near the sea.

quiz.q: Who helps her?
quiz.why: A small crab shows her that she can open her eyes under the water.

quiz.q: Where does she find the big shells?
quiz.why: Under the water she can see where the shells are.

quiz.q: What happens at the end?
options: She eats well and the other birds follow her
quiz.why: She finds food for the whole group, and the others copy her.

roleplay.title: At the sea
roleplay.setting: A windy beach. A mother bird wants her child to find food, and the child does not want to go near the water.

roles.brief: You are patient and hungry. You show your child what to do, and you will not bring the food to her.
You are hungry but scared. You say no to the water, again and again.
You are small, quick and clever. You have a trick, but you cannot explain it in many words.

roleplay.challenge: First round: no English at all, only sounds and actions. Second round: one short sentence for every action.

quest.title: Station 1 · The crab's trick
quest.task: Find the moment the crab helps. What does the little bird do with her eyes, and what can she see?
quest.answer: she opens her eyes under the water and sees the shells

quest.title: Station 2 · Sea words
quest.task: Find the word for water that moves onto the beach, and the word for the tiny stones under your feet.

quest.title: Station 3 · Narrate it
quest.task: Choose thirty seconds of the film. Write three sentences about it, then play the part and check your words.

quest.title: Station 4 · Put it in order
quest.task: Order these four moments: the crab digs, food for all the birds, the big wave, the mother flies off.
quest.answer: mother flies off, the wave, the crab digs, food for all

title: Bao
logline: A lonely mother makes a steamed bun that comes alive, and she raises it as her own child.
why: Eight minutes and almost no dialogue, so the whole class can describe the same pictures together. The story is about family, food and growing up — three topics A1 students can already talk about with very simple words.
language: No English dialogue. A short piece of Mandarin comes from a television in one scene; everything else is music and faces.
content: A dark, sad moment: the mother eats the little bun in despair, and there is no blood — it is a dream. The ending is warm and forgiving.

scenes.title: One bun comes alive
scenes.task: Pause when the bun opens its eyes. What is on the table? Name four things you can see.

scenes.title: Mother and bun
scenes.task: Describe their day in three sentences: what they do, what they eat, where they go.

scenes.title: The girlfriend
scenes.task: The bun brings a girl home. Pause and predict: what will the mother say or do?

scenes.title: The real son
scenes.task: The son comes back. Look at the mother's face. What does she feel, and what does the film say about parents?

words.ex: The mother makes buns in the kitchen.
The bun sits on the kitchen table.
The mother is lonely at home.
Her son comes home at the end.

words.def: to hold someone with your arms
words.ex: They hug and eat together.

words.def: pictures in your head at night
words.ex: The story of the bun is a dream.

questions: What does the mother do with the little bun at the start, and why?
The bun grows up. What does he want to do? Does his mother agree?

title: Wallace & Gromit: A Grand Day Out
logline: Wallace and Gromit have no cheese in the house, so they build a rocket and fly to the moon to find some.
why: There is almost no dialogue: Wallace talks, Gromit answers with his eyebrows, and the story is told by machines and faces. That makes it perfect for A1 — students can narrate the building of the rocket step by step.
language: A few short lines from Wallace in a warm Yorkshire accent, and a lot of silence, music and machine noises; Gromit never speaks.
content: Very mild cartoon danger with a machine on the moon; nothing scary and nobody is hurt. Suitable for all ages.

title: Wallace & Gromit: The Wrong Trousers
logline: Wallace buys a pair of robot trousers and takes in a mysterious penguin lodger, who has a plan for them.
why: The story is almost silent and told through doors, footsteps and machines, so a beginner can follow it without fast speech. Wallace's few lines are short and funny, and the long chase at the end needs no words at all.
language: Short lines from Wallace in a Yorkshire accent and very little else; the penguin says nothing and Gromit says nothing.
content: Cartoon peril: a criminal penguin, a chase on a model railway and a moment where Wallace is in danger. Nobody is hurt and the ending is happy.

title: Shaun the Sheep: The Farmer's Llamas
logline: The Farmer comes home from the fair with three llamas, and the sheep have to share the farm with them.
why: There is almost no dialogue — everything is told by faces, spitting and slapstick — so students can follow without decoding speech. The farm gives a small, repeated set of words (sheep, farmer, dog, gate, house) that an A1 class already knows.
language: Almost no dialogue: animal sounds, music and the odd grunt from the Farmer; the English you hear comes from songs on the radio.
content: Slapstick chaos: animals ride a quad bike, break a fence and lock the Farmer in a wardrobe. Nobody is hurt, and it is played for laughs.
